questions.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes ART, PrEP, and PEP?
choices: ART treats confirmed HIV; PrEP prevents HIV before exposure in people without HIV; PEP is time-sensitive prevention after a possible exposure
They are interchangeable medications for every patient
PEP is long-term HIV treatment
PrEP is used only after an exposure
questions.explanation: These therapies have different purposes and assessment requirements. Correctly defining the goal is the first safety step.

questions.question: Why must HIV status be confirmed before starting PrEP?
choices: PrEP is intended for people without HIV, and unrecognized HIV requires a treatment-focused evaluation
A negative HIV test is never useful
PrEP treats all symptomatic viral illnesses
HIV testing is needed only after adverse effects occur
questions.explanation: CDC guidance requires confirmation that a patient does not have HIV before PrEP initiation. Recent antiretroviral use and acute symptoms can affect testing strategy.

questions.question: A patient seeks care 18 hours after a possible HIV exposure. What is the FNP priority?
choices: Rapidly assess for PEP eligibility and follow the current time-sensitive protocol
Wait several days for all source information before acting
Schedule a routine preventive visit next month
Assume PEP cannot help because the patient has no symptoms
questions.explanation: Potential PEP exposures require rapid evaluation. CDC recommends assessment when a patient presents within 72 hours of an exposure.

questions.question: Why should an FNP review antacids, mineral supplements, and acid-suppression therapy in a patient taking ART?
choices: They can affect absorption or exposure of selected antiretroviral medications
They have no relevance to ART
They replace the need for HIV testing
They automatically cure reflux without any interaction risk
questions.explanation: Some antiretrovirals have clinically significant absorption interactions with acid-reducing agents or products containing polyvalent cations. Check the exact regimen.

questions.question: What is the best response when a patient requests PrEP but does not want to disclose detailed sexual history because of fear of judgment?
choices: Offer stigma-free care, confirm HIV status, complete the required safety assessment, and invite relevant discussion without gatekeeping
Refuse PrEP until every detail is disclosed
Tell the patient PrEP is only for a particular identity group
Document the patient as noncompliant
questions.explanation: CDC recommends informing patients about PrEP and prescribing it to people who request it. Patient-centered, confidential assessment supports safe access.

questions.question: What is an essential part of STI care beyond treating the diagnosed patient?
choices: Discuss partner notification/treatment, prevention, and follow-up or retesting as indicated
Assume treatment removes all reinfection risk
Avoid discussing partners because it is not clinical care
Promise that reporting requirements are identical everywhere
questions.explanation: Partner services can reduce reinfection and transmission. Rules and options, including EPT, vary by jurisdiction and clinical situation.

questions.question: Why should ART not be casually interrupted for a routine side effect or unrelated illness?
choices: Treatment changes require prompt HIV-care review because interruption can have serious consequences
ART has no interaction or adherence considerations
Every side effect means the diagnosis was wrong
A patient can safely substitute any available medication
questions.explanation: ART is individualized. FNP care includes adherence support and interaction review, with timely HIV-care consultation for clinically meaningful changes.

questions.question: Which situation requires trauma-informed, urgent coordinated assessment rather than a routine medication discussion?
choices: Sexual assault or a potential exposure within the PEP time window
A request for a future routine refill
A stable question about health education
A desire to update contact preferences
questions.explanation: PEP is time sensitive, and sexual assault care requires patient-centered urgent assessment, safety planning, and local forensic/reporting processes.

questions.question: What is the safest way to approach HIV/STI confidentiality?
choices: Discuss safe contact methods and privacy honestly, follow applicable law, and do not disclose status without authorization or legal basis
Promise absolute secrecy without considering legal requirements
Tell a partner without the patient’s knowledge in every situation
Use any family phone number for results without asking
questions.explanation: HIV/STI information is sensitive. Communication and reporting must respect patient privacy while following applicable legal and public-health requirements.

questions.question: Why is a complete medication reconciliation important in HIV pharmacology?
choices: Antiretroviral interactions with prescription, nonprescription, supplement, and other exposures can alter efficacy or toxicity
Only HIV medications matter
Interaction review is unnecessary if the patient feels well
Medication lists do not need to include supplements
questions.explanation: ARV drug interactions are common and can increase toxicity or reduce therapeutic response. Review the full regimen using a current interaction resource.
